author: m.kalinin
content: IMO, it makes sense to have that max reorg depth constant defining the min block retention period as well

author: m.kalinin
content: i.e. EL client should retain blocks for at least `REORG_RETENTION_WINDOW`

author: kevaundray
content: Ah I see, copying from zoom: I think the argument was that the reorg depth constant is related to the inactivity leak whereas the cl block retention policy is related to the wsp

author: kevaundray
content:
I _do_ think we can make it the same though and just note that it implies some safety decay constant.

But also just to clarify, I handwaved my way to 8192 epochs based on operational overhead 😄 which was a coincidence

author: kevaundray
content: one month would imply something like safety decay = ~20 I think

author: m.kalinin
content: i am wondering if blocks could become necessery to recover from a long period of non-finality by any means 🤔

author: kevaundray
content: Was going through all the edge cases and ended up noting that for periods of long non-finality, the node should probably hold onto those unfinalised blocks 😄

author: kevaundray
content: This means we decouple historical block serving for checkpoint sync from non-finality related recovery mechanisms

author: kevaundray
content:
It was a wall of text so I wont paste it here, but one edge case I was not able to think through is what happens when a node rejoins the network after 50 days of non-finality (they were offline for the whole 50 days, so they cannot use their local fork-choice data to help them recover)

(It seems that for these very edge casey scenarios, the main solution is to get a checkpoint from an externally trusted source, though admittedly I haven't thought a lot about this)
